newsitem.title: GERMANY: Activists protest against nuclear waste in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Activists protest against nuclear waste in Germany.

text.p: About 1,500 activists in northern Germany demonstrated on Saturday against shipments of nuclear waste to a nearby medium-term storage depot at Gorleben.
Carrying banners with slogans, such as: "Stop nuclear-waste transportation" the protesters gathered in the small town of Dannenberg and marched to the town of Hitzacker 20 km (12 miles) away.
Police said protesters had walked along a quiet stretch of railway and sawed away pieces of the tracks and their foundations. It was not clear much damage had been done.

The spokesman for a local environmental group Wolfgang Ehmke argued that it was too dangerous to transport heavy nuclear waste shipments on rails and bridges had not been built to take the strain of such a weight.
New fears about nuclear shipments were sparked nearly two weeks ago when a train carrying nuclear waste through eastern France was derailed, although officials said there was no radiation leak.

The medium-term nuclear depot and planned long-term dump at Gorleben is a favourite target of the anti-nuclear movement and last year more than 19,000 police and border guards were called in to ensure a shipment reached the plant safely.
The next shipment is planned to arrive there next month.
